$comment: This JSON schema is for any electrical power port

oneOf.description: Constant power loads are typically electronic products - they draw as much power as they need to operate - if the supply voltage falls, the current drawn increases.  Note that this does not mean that the power drawn will not vary, as the appliance does its thing.

LED drivers often have a constant current characteristic, to ensure that all LEDs are equally bright.  The constant current circuit may be integral to the LED lamp, or it may be in a separate LED driver.

Most power supplies and all batteries when discharging are Constant-Voltage.  The voltage will dip a certain amount as the current drawn increases.  The voltage-dip/current ratio can be expressed as a Thevenin resistance.
The oldest type of electrical load, but now limited to electric heaters
Battery charging ports have special coltage/current/time characteristics, specific to each type of battery chemistry.
Input port for cables from solar panels or wind turbine, typically with an MPPT characteristic

The relationship between applied voltage and the current that will flow may be determied by many other factors, including software.  In this case, it will not be possible to predict how much current will flow when something is connected to this port

prechargeProtection.description: When a load is first powered up, any capacitance on the input has to charge extremely rapidly to the supply voltage.  This causes a large inrush current - only limited by the parasitic resistance in the system.  This current spike may damage connectors and switch contacts, and/or cause a momentary dip in the supply voltage experienced by other loads connected to the supply.  Some DC loads include a circuit to limit the initial precharge current, and some supplies require the load to have it.
